title: Help Grace Beat Leukaemia
description: Grace, 21, is fighting high-risk acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL). She urgently needs an allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant to survive.

story.intro: Grace is a 21-year-old medical student at the University of Manchester who was diagnosed with high-risk Philadelphia chromosome-positive Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (Ph+ ALL). She urgently needs an allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant to have a chance at long-term survival. While the NHS covers her standard treatment, the cost of faster private access, travel, relocation near her specialist centre, and lost income has become overwhelming for her family.

sections.title: The Diagnosis
sections.content:
It all started in March 2026, when Grace began experiencing intense weakness, petechiae on her legs, and frequent febrile episodes. On 20th March, after a blood panel showed pancytopenia and suspicious blast cells, she was rushed to the Haematology Department at The Christie NHS Foundation Trust in Manchester.

Bone marrow biopsy and molecular analysis confirmed the diagnosis: B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (B-ALL), with the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene (Philadelphia chromosome positive). This is an aggressive form of leukaemia that requires intensive therapy and a transplant for long-term survival.

sections.title: The Treatment Protocol
sections.content:
Grace immediately began induction therapy with the HyperCVAD protocol combined with a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI — dasatinib) due to her Ph+ status. After two cycles of chemotherapy, she has achieved complete haematologic remission and minimal residual disease (MRD) is now measured at levels < 0.01%.

Her doctors recommend an allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant from a matched donor to consolidate the remission. Her younger sister, Hannah, has been found to be a perfect HLA match (10/10 compatibility) and has already agreed to be the donor.

sections.title: Why We Need Your Help
sections.content: We want to be completely transparent. Grace's core treatment — chemotherapy, the TKI, and the transplant itself — is provided by the NHS at The Christie. But the NHS cannot cover everything quickly enough, and several options that could save Grace's life are simply not available on the NHS or carry waiting times she does not have.
coveredItems: Induction and consolidation chemotherapy (HyperCVAD) — The Christie
Tyrosine kinase inhibitor (dasatinib) for Ph+ status
Allogeneic stem cell transplant + donor workup (Hannah)
Hospitalisation in a positive-pressure isolation room
sections.notCoveredLabel: Not Available on the NHS / Requires Private Access
notCoveredItems: Next-generation TKIs (ponatinib) if resistance develops — restricted NHS access and long approval delays
Biologic therapies if relapse occurs (blinatumomab, inotuzumab) — limited NHS funding for Ph+ ALL
MRD monitoring by NGS sequencing — not routinely funded, private labs only
Private or overseas treatment to avoid NHS waiting times if the disease progresses
Family relocation and living expenses near The Christie during 6+ months post-transplant
Loss of income while both parents are on extended leave to care for Grace

items.text: Private next-generation TKIs and biologic therapies (if relapse/resistance)

quote.text: I wanted to become a doctor to help people. Now I'm the one in the hospital bed, and I understand how important it is when strangers show up for you. Every donation isn't just money — it's a chance to keep dreaming. I promise you, when I beat this, I will spend my life helping patients who are going through what I'm going through right now.
quote.author: Grace W.

updates.title: Positive news from molecular testing! 💪
updates.content: The latest RT-PCR results are encouraging — BCR-ABL levels are below 0.01%! Her doctors at The Christie are very pleased with the treatment response. The transplant is scheduled for late August. Her sister Hannah is already completing preliminary donor testing.

updates.title: We've passed 600 donors! 🙏
updates.content: We have no words to express our gratitude. Grace has completed the second cycle of chemotherapy and her doctors have confirmed complete haematologic remission. Every pound brings us closer to the transplant.

updates.title: Update from the hospital
updates.content: Grace has completed the first cycle of chemotherapy at The Christie. She had neutropenia after treatment, but she was smiling while reading your messages. The nurses brought her a small celebration in her room. Your response has moved us deeply.

updates.title: The campaign has launched
updates.content: With heavy hearts but also with hope, we're launching this appeal for help. After two months of intensive therapy, her doctors have confirmed that the transplant is the only option for a long-term cure. Even with the NHS covering the core treatment, the financial toll on our family has been devastating. We believe in the power of community.
